vision_features.image_context: The image shows multiple broad, ovate leaves of a low-growing plant, viewed from above. The plant appears to have trifoliate or simple broad leaves typical of a bean-type plant. Multiple leaves at various canopy levels are visible, along with bare soil beneath. Both upper leaf surfaces and some undersides are visible.
vision_features.abnormalities:
1. Upper leaf surface — pale whitish-gray to silvery patches: Located across the upper surface of most leaves, particularly concentrated toward the center and spreading outward. Size ranges from small (5–10 mm) to large confluent areas covering 30–50% of some leaf surfaces. Shape is diffuse and irregular, not sharply defined. Color is a pale grayish-white to silvery-white, contrasting against the normal green. No distinct darker border or halo visible around patches. Texture appears slightly dusty or faintly powdery on closer areas; surface appears matte and faded compared to healthy tissue. No discrete raised structures or tiny dots visible within the pale patches themselves. Distribution is widespread across most visible leaves, affecting both younger and older leaves, more severe on lower-canopy leaves.
2. Small reddish-brown to tan spots: Scattered across some leaf surfaces, particularly visible on the lower-right and central leaves. Size is pinpoint to small (1–3 mm). Shape is roughly circular to irregular. Color is tan to light brown with no obvious distinct border. Texture appears dry and flat. Distribution is scattered, not clustered densely, interspersed among the larger pale patches.
3. General leaf surface discoloration: Several leaves show an overall dull, grayish-green tone rather than bright green, affecting the broad interveinal areas. The veins retain somewhat greener coloration compared to interveinal tissue, giving a subtle mottled appearance on some leaves.
vision_features.absences: 1. No visible yellowing (yellow coloration) surrounding or adjacent to the pale patches — margins of affected areas remain greenish or fade to gray-white without a yellow halo. 2. No obvious raised pustules or blister-like raised structures visible on either leaf surface. 3. No wilting, curling, or distortion of the leaf margins or overall leaf shape is apparent. 4. No visible thread-like growths, fuzzy coating, or obvious surface mycelial mass protruding from the leaf surface.
vision_features.summary: The most prominent feature across the majority of visible leaves is the presence of large, diffuse, pale whitish-gray to silvery patches covering significant portions of the upper leaf surfaces, giving many leaves a washed-out or bleached appearance. The leaves most severely affected are those in the mid and lower canopy layers. Secondary small reddish-brown dry spots are scattered across some leaf surfaces. The most striking visual feature is the widespread silvery-gray bleaching of the interveinal areas across nearly all visible leaves, with the veins retaining relatively more green coloration, creating a subtle mottled pattern.
